long_description:
Our South Asian communities have always been diverse, complex, and evolving. Long before colonization, many South Asian societies recognized gender identities beyond the binary and made space for expansive understandings of gender.

Yet today, transgender, nonbinary, and genderqueer people often face stigma, exclusion, and misunderstanding within our own families and communities.

At a time when transphobia, anti-trans violence, and anti-trans legislation are on the rise, silence is political.

Creating safety for transgender and gender-expansive people is not a passive process. It requires us to listen, learn, show up, and take responsibility for the communities we are building.

Join us on Friday, November 13, for a community conversation centering trans and genderqueer South Asian stories, safety, and belonging.

Together, we will hear from transgender, nonbinary, and genderqueer artists, practitioners, activists, and community leaders whose work reflects a deep commitment to justice, belonging, and collective care.

The evening will also include creative offerings rooted in storytelling, resistance, joy, and community.
